title: Suspect in theft of 2 vehicles worth $395K from Ferrari of Greenwich 'in the wind,' prosecutor says - NewsBreak
text: STAMFORD — One of several people accused of stealing two luxury vehicles from a Greenwich Ferrari dealership has effectively disappeared following an arrest as a fugitive of justice earlier this month, according to state prosecutors. Lauren Webb, 27, was scheduled to appear at the state Superior Court in Stamford Wednesday in connection with the theft of two Mercedes-Benz G-Class vehicles valued at a total of $395,000 from Ferrari of Greenwich on West Putnam Avenue in November 2023. But when her case was called Wednesday morning, both her attorney Thomas Cocco and Assistant State’s Attorney Michelle Manning made a startling admission: nobody knew where the defendant was. Manning explained that Webb was recently arrested by Milford police as a fugitive of justice after she failed to appear in Florida on an unrelated case. But in the wake of her arrest, Manning said there is no record of her being incarcerated in Connecticut, nor is there any record of her having been extradited to Florida. One possible explanation for this, Manning explained, is that Webb posted bond and is free. What is complicating matters, according to Manning, is that Webb is supposed to be on GPS monitoring, and if she was released from custody, she was let go without the appropriate monitoring device. “I think the concern is that we don’t know where she is,” Manning said. “She’s out in the wind, essentially.” Webb’s case was given a short continuance to Monday as both attorneys try to track her down. If she isn’t located by then, Manning said she would ask a judge to order a rearrest. Webb is the latest of three suspects arrested in connection with the Greenwich luxury car thefts. Reheem Spencer, 28, and Shemoya Gayle, 20, were also charged in the case. All three face conspiracy to commit first-degree larceny charges. In addition to the Greenwich thefts, the Webb and her codefendants are suspected of more than $1 million in car thefts across the country , according to their arrest warrants. But police believe the Ferrari of Greenwich dealer was just one of many stops in a grand theft auto scheme that spanned several states and resulted in more than $900,000 worth of car thefts. According to arrest warrants, Webb, Gayle, Spencer and an unidentified individual ran similar schemes in at least two other states, and were spotted allegedly casing dealerships in even more locations. “This group may also be responsible for the recent thefts of two Lamborghinis from McLaren of Boston and for visiting Lamborghini of Philadelphia on November 28, 2023,” Greenwich police Detective Chris LiBasci wrote in a warrant. Detective Ken Camerota of the Norwell Police Department in Massachusetts confirmed on Wednesday that Gayle, Spencer and others are lead suspects in a similar scheme that led to the theft of two Lamborghinis — a Huracan and a Urus, collectively valued at around $500,000 — from McLaren of Boston a day earlier than the Greenwich thefts. Camerota said the suspects perpetrated a similar scheme to the one used in Greenwich. Individuals pretending to be potential buyers went into the McLaren dealer earlier in the day, he said. During the visit, police believe they pocketed the key fobs to two Lamborghinis, then left fake fobs in their place. Later that night, the suspects came back to the dealer and swiped the cars, which were recovered months later in Texas, according to Camerota. “They had to have had the car fobs, because we didn’t see any evidence of break-in in our review of the surveillance footage,” Camerota said. Unfortunately, Camerota said, the footage from the dealership hasn’t been enough to obtain arrest warrants in the case, so the investigation remains ongoing. After striking in Massachusetts, the group of at least four headed to Greenwich, where they were spotted on camera not only staking out Ferrari of Greenwich but several other local high-end dealerships, as well. Greenwich Det. Christopher LiBasci wrote in the warrants that Gayle and Webb were seen on camera on Nov. 25, 2023 — the day the car thefts occurred — also entering McLaren of Greenwich and Rolls Royce of Greenwich, both of which also are owned and operated by Miller MotorCars. A fourth, unidentified woman also was seen that day entering Lamborghini of Greenwich, the owners of which told police that they also spotted members of the group at their Lamborghini of Philadelphia location three days later, the warrants said. Earlier that year, in July 2023, Gayle, Spencer and Webb all were detained in Pickens County, Ga., for “racing and driving recklessly” in a stolen BMW worth nearly $80,000, police said in the warrant. In that incident, Gayle and Webb confessed to swapping fake keys with the real ones at the Georgia dealership to steal the car, which Greenwich police said mirrored the theft pulled off at Miller Motorcars Ferrari. After being arrested, Gayle told police that she had agreed to steal the car in return for $2,000 from Webb, the warrant said.
